title: Local dimension and regularity of a DVR binomial surface
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ and residue field $k=R/(\pi)$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. For $e\ge1$ set $A_e=R[x,y]/(xy-\pi^e)$ and $M_e=\operatorname{Spec}A_e$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These rings are Noetherian and flat over $R$; the presentation is finite [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Every local ring of $M_e$ has dimension at most two, and at $o=(\pi,x,y)$ its dimension is two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The two opens $D(x)$ and $D(y)$ cover $M_e\setminus\{o\}$, their coordinate rings are Laurent polynomial rings over $R$, and all their local rings are regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Put $P=R[x,y]_{(\pi,x,y)}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. This is a regular local ring of dimension three, the classes of $\pi,x,y$ are a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, and $f=xy-\pi^e$ is nonzero. For $e=1$ its maximal-adic order is one, with initial form $-\Pi$; for $e=2$ its order is two with initial form $XY-\Pi^2$; for $e>2$ its order is two with initial form $XY$ in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}P=k[\Pi,X,Y]$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. The quotient local ring $P/(f)=\mathcal O_{M_e,o}$ is regular exactly for $e=1$, with cotangent dimension two in that case and three otherwise. No completeness, excellence or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Write $B=R[x,y]$ and $\mathfrak q=(\pi,x,y)$. The DVR definition makes $R$ a Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $(\pi)$. Its dimension is one by lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one; hence it is regular local by the definition of regularity, and regular as a ring by regular-local localization. The polynomial theorems therefore make $B$ a Noetherian regular domain of dimension $1+2=3$. In particular $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, with quotient $k$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), Tags 00KU and 0AFS (definition-regular-local, lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular), Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); polynomial regularity and dimension supplied by the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: Apply the binomial normal-form lemma with $a=\pi^e\ne0$: the monomials $1,x^i,y^j$ ($i,j>0$) form an $R$-basis of $A_e$. Thus if a nonzero scalar kills an element, it kills each coefficient and that element is zero. The PID torsion-free flatness theorem gives $R$-flatness. The two generators and single relation give finite presentation, and finite-type Noetherian permanence gives Noetherianity of $A_e$. The polynomial $f=xy-\pi^e$ is nonzero because its $xy$ coefficient is $1$; its image in $P=B_{\mathfrak q}$ remains nonzero, since a fraction $f/1=0$ would imply $sf=0$ for a nonzero $s\notin\mathfrak q$ in the domain $B$.

proof.text:
The local ring $P$ is regular because $B$ is regular. Its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qP$ is generated by $\pi,x,y$, and its residue field is $k$. The prime chain $(0)\subsetneq(\pi)\subsetneq(\pi,x)\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ in $B$ has length three: the successive quotient rings are $B$, $k[x,y]$, $k[y]$, $k$, all domains, and strictness follows respectively from $\pi
e0$, $x
e0$ in $k[x,y]$, and $y
e0$ in $k[y]$. The localization dimension/chains theorem and $\dim B=3$ give $\dim P=3$. The cotangent-dimension theorem now gives $\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=3$. Its three spanning classes $\pi,x,y$ consequently form a basis.

proof.text:
Apply the regular-hypersurface initial-form lemma to the regular local ring $P$ and $0
e f\in\mathfrak m$. Its graded isomorphism identifies the classes of $\pi,x,y$ with $\Pi,X,Y$ in $k[\Pi,X,Y]$. If $e=1$, the degree-one component of $f$ is $-\Pi
e0$, since $xy\in\mathfrak m^2$. If $e=2$, its degree-two component is $XY-\Pi^2
e0$. If $e>2$, then $\pi^e\in\mathfrak m^3$ and that component is $XY
e0$. These are nonzero polynomials in every characteristic, being nonzero monomials or a difference of distinct monomials. Thus the orders are respectively one, two and two. The same lemma gives $\dim P/(f)=2$, cotangent dimensions two for $e=1$ and three for $e>1$, and regularity exactly when $e=1$. Localization of a quotient identifies $P/(f)$ with $(A_e)_o$; the affine stalk theorem identifies this with $\mathcal O_{M_e,o}$.

proof.text: For any prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A_e$, take a strict chain of length $t$ of primes of $A_e$ contained in $\mathfrak p$. Inverse image under $B\twoheadrightarrow A_e$ is a strict chain of length $t$ of primes of $B$ containing $f$: primality follows by lifting products, and strictness by lifting an element in each ideal difference. Its first prime is nonzero because it contains $f\ne0$. Prepending the prime $(0)$ of the domain $B$ gives a chain of length $t+1$. Since $\dim B=3$, $t\le2$. The localization dimension/chains theorem and the affine stalk theorem give $\dim\mathcal O_{M_e,\mathfrak p}\le2$. This includes nonclosed points and primes over the generic point, without a catenarity assumption.

proof.text: A prime of $A_e$ containing both $x$ and $y$ contains $\pi^e=xy$, hence $\pi$; it is therefore $o$, since $A_e/(\pi,x,y)=k$. Conversely $o$ contains both. Thus $D(x)\cup D(y)=M_e\setminus\{o\}$. The principal-open affine localization theorem and the normal-form lemma identify their coordinate rings with $R[x,x^{-1}]$ and $R[y,y^{-1}]$: on the first chart $y=\pi^e x^{-1}$, and on the second $x=\pi^e y^{-1}$. Here $R[t,t^{-1}]$ means $R[t][1/t]$. The polynomial regular-base theorem makes $R[t]$ regular, and localization preserves regular rings, so both Laurent rings are regular. By the affine stalk theorem, every local ring on these two opens is a prime localization of one of these regular rings and is regular local. No step used completeness, excellence or a restriction on the characteristic.
